sections.section_name: Section B - Theory Short Answer Concepts

questions.question_text: What is a portrait, and what is the most important proportion to keep in mind when drawing a human face? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: A portrait is a painting or drawing focusing on a person's face. The most important proportion is that the eyes are typically located exactly in the middle of the head, halfway between the chin and the top of the head.

questions.question_text: How can adding texture change the mood or feel of a simple pencil drawing? Give one example. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Texture makes a flat drawing look realistic and tactile. For example, adding rough, crisscross pencil strokes to a tree trunk makes the bark look rough, aged, and natural.

questions.question_text: Define 'Raga' in Indian music. How is it different from a simple tune? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: A Raga is a specific melodic framework or scale using a defined set of notes in Indian classical music. Unlike a simple tune, a Raga creates a specific mood or emotion and has strict rules for ascending and descending notes.

questions.question_text: What is a motif, and how is it used to create a repeated pattern in textile design? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A motif is a single basic design element, like a flower or geometric shape. When a motif is repeated continuously in a grid or sequence, it creates a pattern.

questions.question_text: Classify musical instruments into two broad categories based on how they produce sound, providing one example for each. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Instruments can be classified as string instruments (Chordophones), which produce sound by plucking or bowing strings, like the Sitar; and percussion instruments (Membranophones), which produce sound by striking a stretched skin, such as the Tabla.

sections.section_name: Section C - Practical Tasks: Composition & Observation

questions.question_text: Arrange and draw a still life composition of three fresh vegetables (e.g., a brinjal, a tomato, and a capsicum) resting on a cloth drape. Shade the arrangement using the cross-hatching technique. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Checklist: Accurate observation of vegetable shapes and sizes relative to each other earns highest points. Effective use of cross-hatching to define volume and the light source, along with proper rendering of the cloth folds and the cast shadow grounding the objects, completes the scoring.

questions.question_text: Observe and sketch a detailed nature study of a large tree branch with at least five overlapping leaves, focusing carefully on the vein textures and organic curves. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Precision in capturing the organic curves of the leaves and accurate overlapping without looking stiff earns maximum marks. Detailed rendering of the central and secondary veins, along with varying tonal values to show leaf depth, will determine the final grade.

sections.section_name: Section D - Practical Tasks: Applied Design & Messaging

questions.question_text: Design a colorful and impactful poster on the theme 'Water is Life' using poster colors. Include a catchy slogan and relevant visual elements in a balanced layout. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Scoring Breakdown: Visual impact and relevance to the water conservation theme are prioritized. Clean, legible block lettering for the slogan is essential. Smooth application of poster colors without muddying, and overall layout balance ensuring the central illustration of water drops or the earth is perfectly centered and proportional, complete the evaluation.

questions.question_text: Design an attractive book cover for a collection of Indian folk tales. Use traditional Indian motifs and a stylized title font in a vertical rectangular layout. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Checklist: Integration of traditional Indian motifs (like paisley, lotus, or mandala elements) in the border or background earns high marks. Creativity in designing a stylized, readable title font, selecting a harmonious color palette suitable for folk tales, and neatness in utilizing the vertical rectangular space dictate the final score.
